## Rule

Input: 30×30 grid, several non-bg colors. ONE color (the "target") forms a single
compact connected blob (≤5 rows/cols); the other colors are scattered noise.
Output: the bounding box of the target blob, target-color cells preserved, other
cells set to 0 (variable output shape = the bbox). The generator's exact selector
is "the color with exactly 1 connected component of size>1" (numpy ref, 267/267).
The canonical ONNX approximates this with "the only present color whose row-span
fits in 5" (base-16 positional score) — correct on ~199998/200000 (see Don't-do:
2 fresh-gen cases where a span-6 noise color is mis-selected). Builder: numpy ref
at `task036/prototypes/task036_numpy_reference.py`.

## Algorithm sketch

```
for each non-bg color: components = 4-connected blobs of that color
target = the color with exactly one component of size>1   # scattered noise = many size-1 comps
out = bbox(target_component) with target color at its cells, 0 elsewhere
```

## Cost analysis

v4 (1016) charged-tensor breakdown: per-color base-16 score vectors `[10] F32` ×4 = 160 B (target selection, intrinsic to the rule); `v1_shifted_target [1,1,5,5] F32` = 100 B (the crop); `v1_out_crop_bool [1,10,5,5] BOOL` = 250 B (one-hot crop expansion, 2nd largest); `v1_bbox_mask [1,1,5,5] BOOL` = 25 B; Slice geometry `v4_slice_starts/ends [3] INT64` = 48 B (REPLACED v1's 600 B GatherND index + 48 B offset chain). The single highest-leverage cut was GatherND→Slice (-600 B memory). params 101 = coord weights `[30]×2`=60 + channel_vals[10]=10 + pad_pads[8]=8 + range5[5]=5 + reshape consts[4]×2=8 + slice geom[3]×2=6 + 4 scalars. Further down: aditya's net (1625) drops the 250 B one-hot-crop by producing the full-canvas output via one final free-output Einsum instead of Pad — a possible follow-up, but its statistical target rule is heavier; not pursued this session.

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._
- Treat `task036_v2_gather_bbox_coords_20260516` as the reviewed queue candidate; future task036 work should be a strictly cheaper/new-behavior continuation, not a duplicate review or resubmit of the same ONNX/package.
- **Don't chase the 2/200k truth gap by swapping to a "robust" integer selector at this cost class.** The canonical v1/v4 base-16 row-span score (`min_row_score * max_row_score`) UNDERFLOWS when the target blob sits at high row indices, so the span≤5 test misfires and a span-6 noise color is picked over the true span-4 target (1 confirmed fresh-ARC-GEN input: color1 rows2-7 span6 cnt7 vs color2 rows7-10 span4 cnt13 → v4 picks wrong). v5 (`build_task036_v5_robust.py`) replaces this with integer ReduceMax/ArgMax per-color row/col spans + smallest-bbox-area ArgMin. It IS robust on that case but (a) costs **9216** — the six `[1,10,30,1]`/`[1,10,1,30]` per-color mask reductions are 1200 B each — so it loses to aditya's 1625, and (b) the smallest-area heuristic STILL misses a *different* 1/200k case (199999 truth). True 100% needs aditya's exact connected-component/moment rule, which at best ties aditya's 1625 — no cost win. **aditya owns the 100%-correct niche @1625; v4 owns the cheap niche @1016 byte-equal to the current ship. Ship v4; leave the edge case to aditya.**
- v5 robust-integer-select: cost 9216, truth 199999 — REJECTED (worse than v4 on cost AND not 100% correct). Builder kept at `task036/prototypes/build_task036_v5_robust.py` as the documented dead-end.
- **Don't pursue the free-output Einsum tail (delete the 250 B one-hot crop) to beat v4's 1016 — it cannot win on THIS task.** v6 (`build_task036_v6_freeout.py`, profiled 2026-06-21) is byte-equal to v4 (200265/200265, truth 199998) and structurally clean, yet lands at **1193 (+177)**. Two independent reasons, both irreducible: (1) The 5→30 canvas-placement basis `[5,30]` is charged **150 params** as an initializer (element count, dtype-agnostic — traps §15). There is NO cheaper static basis for placing a 5-wide crop into a 30-canvas, and generating it (EyeLike) costs ≥300–600 B of surviving intermediate memory (no F16/bool kernel; zero_param_generators caveat) — worse than 150 stored params. (2) Deleting the 250 B `v1_out_crop_bool` does NOT lower memory: the Einsum requires materializing the spatial-term stack `[2,5,5]` + the F16 crop/bbox planes (~400 B total), which replaces the crop byte-for-byte (v6 mem 932 ≥ v4 mem 915). The mission's lever (250 B crop = v4's top intermediate, 27.3%) was correctly identified but the *replacement* cost (placement basis + factor fan-out) exceeds the saving. aditya's 1625 net uses this same free-output Einsum but pays for it elsewhere (heavier statistical target rule); the technique only wins when there's NO cheap Pad alternative AND no placement-basis param cost. For task036, v4's `Equal`+BOOL-`Pad` tail IS the floor. Builder kept at `task036/prototypes/build_task036_v6_freeout.py` as documented dead-end.
